symptom: `column (Attribute: IsActive) { dropdownfilter ddf (defaultValue: 'true') }` passed check and exec, then mx check failed CE0117 "Error(s) in expression." at the drop-down filter (mendixlabs/mxcli#1611 B).
cause: defaultValue is a pluggable Expression property whose template declares ReturnType String, and a quoted MDL value on an Expression property is the expression's text, so 'true' stored the Boolean expression `true`. No check typed an authored expression against the property's declared return type; the embedded schema read each property's ValueType.Type but not its ReturnType.
fix: MDL-WIDGET49 (validate_widget_expression_return.go), beside MDL-WIDGET42 in validateWidgetProperties: for a String-returning Expression property, refuse a value that infers as a literal Boolean, Integer or Decimal (exprcheck.InferSourceKind) or is one bare name, with the String-literal spelling as the hint (`defaultValue: '''true'''`). embeddedWidgetSchema.returns records ReturnType.Type per Expression key. Runs with and without a project (the DROPDOWNFILTER definition is built in).
insight: The writer was right and the check was missing: the MDL convention (a quoted value IS the expression text) is what describe prints and what every other expression property relies on, so 'wrap the string for a String-returning property' would have silently changed the meaning of every existing script. Measure the column type separately from the property's return type: '1' failed in an Integer column too — the return type is the widget's, fixed at String, not the attribute's. Judge only what InferSourceKind is sure of: it calls [%CurrentDateTime%] a String, so DateTime is not trusted; Unknown (paths, variables, untyped functions) is never refused.
